findings.evidenceType: manual local source pixels and actual-size browser states
findings.finding: Brown body, rusty face/undertail, short conical bill and long tail remain recognizable as the intended California Towhee. The bird reads consistently across new poses and reused neutral at the declared size. Dense pale/tan feather detailing persists in native and output art; it gives the body a textured appearance rather than a quiet flat interior. It was not an obvious gross brightness flash in reviewed states. This is not evidence that the unseen Mac mottling issue is fixed or caused by these sources.

Crouch substantially lowers/compresses the body, airborne toes curl up, descending legs/toes extend, and settle returns to support. Four real body/leg drawings plus one existing neutral are visible. Separate authored translation makes the viewer travel backward while facing right. This is one hop, not a complete double-scratch, peck, leaf scratch or feeding sequence.

Tucked toes are densely curled/overlapping and leg/toe contours are angular at small output. No obvious detached major limb or additional major leg was apparent. Native low-alpha colored edge residue is visible against black enlargement; no conspicuous broad halo was apparent against the reviewed pale normal background. External anatomical expert approval and other-background alpha behavior remain pending.

findings.evidenceType: manual all five source states and live samples
findings.finding: The strong crouch and supported settle have lower, more horizontal silhouettes than the upright reused neutral. This makes the compression/settle-to-neutral changes conspicuous, but pose compression is not itself a scale failure. Head, bill, rusty regions and long tail remain coherent enough for a bounded hop study; the motion is stepped rather than a smooth complete cycle. No per-pose bbox fit or exact-bodyRGBA quality requirement was imposed.

findings.evidenceType: manual enlarged/normal samples plus independent heuristic shape diagnostics
findings.finding: One primary lower-toe boundary is consistently registered, while other toes change spacing, silhouette and shape. At actual presentation those stance changes are visible as short toe redraw during compression/settle/neutral return; the action may be acceptable provisionally, but it is not evidence that every planted toe stays fixed. The approximately1.90worldpx combined-foot centroid difference and3.162outputpx mask Hausdorff distance quantify shape change, not a rigid translation of the whole foot.
